title: When the Passage Falls
premise: Salvage diver Marguerite Winterbourne recovers a sealed chest from a wreck the navy has quietly written off, and inside finds documents proving the river's shipping concessions were built on a forged inheritance that dispossessed an entire river community. Hunted by the concession company's enforcers and shadowed by a navy officer with his own guilty stake in the cover-up, she assembles a makeshift crew of divers, smugglers, and the heir the forgery erased. Racing upstream against expiring permits and rising water, they reach the forbidden source where the original deed is hidden. Marguerite floods the company's records into the public record at the source itself, winning justice for the community — and discovering the family she never measured in miles.
about_author: Kestrel Dunmore is the pen name of a former maritime surveyor who spent a decade charting inland waterways before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people who trust rivers more than institutions.

chapters.title: The Chest That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Diving a navy-scrubbed wreck, she raises a chest stamped with the seal of a nation dissolved decades ago, containing a forged inheritance deed and a map to the river's source. The navy demands she surrender it; instead she hides it. Emotional beat: wary curiosity hardening into defiance as she realizes the wreck was no accident.

chapters.title: Crew of the Dispossessed
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, with interludes from navy officer Callum Reyes. She recruits Tomas, grandson of the family the forgery erased, plus a smuggler pilot and an archivist who can read the old seals. Company enforcers burn her boat. Emotional beat: strangers becoming something like crew, grief for her lost livelihood transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Upstream Against the Clock
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Marguerite and Callum, who defects after finding his own name on the cover-up ledger. The crew runs rapids, evades patrol boats, and deciphers the map as permits expire and flood season rises. An ambush costs them their supplies and nearly Tomas. Emotional beat: trust tested under pressure; Callum's guilt becomes commitment.

chapters.title: Where the River Begins
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At the forbidden source, they find the original deed hidden in a drowned chapel. Enforcers corner them, but Marguerite broadcasts scans of both deeds to every port office downstream before the water takes the originals. The concession collapses; the community's claim stands. Emotional beat: justice won outside the law, and Marguerite choosing to stay — a life finally measured in people, not miles.
